reason: The hypothesis makes several specific mechanistic claims about grain boundary character effects in tungsten alloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers general grain boundary behavior, but the specific claims about tungsten at 1200–1500°C and the engineering of boundary character require supporting citations which are absent.
premises: High-angle grain boundaries promote dislocation climb and grain boundary sliding at high temperatures
Low-angle grain boundaries impede dislocation motion
Grain boundary sliding increases plastic strain but reduces toughness
Dislocation climb is a dominant deformation mechanism in tungsten at 1200–1500°C
Grain boundary character can be engineered independently of grain size
